faq.a: Saima is associated with the Arabic form صَائِمَة, whose core sense is saima; fasting (feminine).

faq.q: What is the origin of Saima?
faq.a: Saima is associated with Arabic. Saima is Arabic صَائِمَة (Ṣāʾima), the feminine active participle of صَامَ, meaning 'one who fasts'.
Yes — the underlying form صَائِمَة is Arabic.
Saima can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Saima should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ص و م is Quranic (fasting), but Ṣāʾima is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Saima mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Saima is rendered صائمہ and carries the sense صائمہ، روزہ رکھنے والی.

faq.q: What does Saima mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Saima is rendered صائمه and carries the sense صائمه، روزه‌دار.
A romanized syllable approximation is sai-ma. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Saima?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Saima, saima. Script forms are صائمه, صائمہ, صَائِمَة, साइमा.

faq.q: Is Saima a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
